COMMUNITY ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA  
 
 
 
Treat according to clinical judgment &  
CURB 65 Severity Score 
SUSPECTED PNEUMONIA 
* History 
* Clinical examination 
* Radiographic findings 
CURB65 Severity Score 
1 point for each feature present 
* Confusion 
* Urea ≥ 7mmol 
* Respiratory Rate ≥ 30/min 
* Blood Pressure 
   SBP ≤ 90mmHg / DBP ≤ 60mmHg 
* Age ≥ 65 years 
CURB 65 Severity Score 0 - 1 
(risk of death < 3%) 
 
Other reasons for admission?                     
eg. unstable comorbidities, poor social 
circumstances, no transport? 
 
   No                           Yes 
 
 
 
      Discharge Home 
 
 
Augmentin 375mg + 
Amoxil 500mg x 5/7 
± 
Erythromycin 500mg 
qid po x 5/7 (if atypical 
features on xrays) 
If Augmentin out of 
stock: Amoxil 1g tds 
po x 5/7 
If Penicillin Allergy: 
Erythromycin 500mg 
qid po x 5/7 
 
Admit 
Management as for 
Severity Score 2 
Refer to Resp 
*If TB infection is 
suspected-advise 
sputum AFB's & 
GXP 
If Age > 65 years is the only criteria - Follow for 
Severity Score 2 as renal dysfunction likely 
CURB 65 Severity Score 2 
(risk of death < 9%) 
 
Hospital Admission – refer to Resp 
 
 
* Supportive Care e.g. oxygen, IV fluids 
* Bloods: FBC/U+E/CRP 
* Initiate early IV antibiotic therapy 
 
 
 Augmentin 1.2g IV stat 
± 
Azithromycin 500mg po/IV 
if 
           
  * Atypical features on xray 
  *  Elderly 
            
  * COPD exacerbation 2° bacterial infection 
CURB 65 Severity Score 3 - 5 
(risk of death 15-40%) 
 
Urgent Hospital Admission – refer to Resp 
 
 
                                            
* Supportive Care  e.g. oxygen, IV fluids 
* Intubate if required 
* Bloods: ABG/FBC/U+E/CRP/Blood cultures 
* Initiate early IV antibiotic therapy 
 
Augmentin 1.2g IV stat / Zinacef 1.5g IV stat 
AND 
Azithromycin 500mg po/IV 
AND 
Hydrocortisone 100mg IVI stat 
 
 
 CURB 65 4-5  
  ICU/High Care Admission – refer to Resp 
 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
